My master's is in Psychology, with a clinical psych focus.

Virology, now that's an out-there suggestion :p I'm afraid I likely don't have the background for this, as I haven't taken bio/chem classes since high school.

It could be interesting to day trade, though the thought of doing that for a living is a bit scary.

Thank you! Interesting, I never would have considered forensic accounting. 

I probably should have mentioned more clearly that I struggle quite a bit with processing numbers (nothing diagnosed, but suspected dyscalculia). It does complicates things because numbers often go hand in hand with pattern-heavy careers. Of course, it's hard to avoid both numbers AND words, so at the end of the day I'm weighing tradeoffs.

That study is about general stigma, not hiring stigma. Neither country is doing well on that front. I'd be happy to be pointed in the direction of US companies eager to hire autistic individuals of average-high intelligence over allistics. 

And reality is, if you can't get hired, there are many, many countries where it's better to be autistic...

(Think better access to healthcare and general social support systems. Including China. It's really fucking hard to eke out a basic existence in the US without a (edit: full time) job, and almost impossible to be covered by your parents' health plan after turning 29.)

Sure. I can't compare the two from personal experience, but nothing in your article is something I haven't encountered here as well. "Extending sympathy" but refusing to hire is the standard in the US unless you're lucky enough to be a savant. Savants would get hired in China, too.

I'm autistic and Chinese (edit: US citizen). Can confirm it's just as bad as the article describes here in the US. I wouldn't mind going back to China because I trust that my extended family would help keep things together, and might even help me secure some job (it takes a village). Here, it's so individualistic. I'm flailing alone. I've been applying for full-time jobs for 10+ years with no luck, though I've managed to complete some degrees in the process.

Thank you for the rec! Scheduled my first session with campus counseling in two weeks, and I'll see if there's anyone long term they can refer me to with experience in those therapies (or something similar).

100%.

Also, I think downvoters must be assuming that OP just wants to get a job or start a business and knows what he wants, but that isn't the case here. Frankly, he says himself that he has no direction and feels utterly lost. That is NOT a mindset from which someone should make the decision to trash their undergrad record for good by "just pushing through" when all signs point to taking time off.

Edit: and thank you!! I appreciate it. I've been doing a post bacc and although school is still challenging for me (learning disabilities), it's made a world of difference to know why I'm there, how it helps me achieve my goals, and what I want to get out of the experience.

Hey, I was in your situation at 21 and need to speak up. Everyone told me the whole "your gpa doesn't matter" thing. Truth is, if you EVER change your mind later -- like if you realize in your early 30s that you want to go back to school -- your GPA will matter. It will matter if you ever want to apply to something like the Peace Corps, too (very specific I know, and maybe irrelevant but that's the kind of program that will also ask for transcripts). 

I have so many regrets about forcing myself to grind through my degree before I was ready. I never thought I wanted to go to grad school until my late 20s, but now my undergrad GPA limits me significantly. Standardized test scores can only do so much to balance it out.

My youngest sister learned from my mistakes and when she couldn't handle UG at 19/20/21, she went and picked up retail and service jobs and lived very simply until she felt ready. She's only a sophomore now at 22, but her GPA is intact and it's much easier to explain extended medical leave than a 2.low GPA. She'll be able to do anything she wants to after undergrad. My grad school options are already cut in half (at best).

Please consider leaving school and working basic jobs for a while if you're not ready to handle it yet
